The sleeve that excelled in all these criteria were from the Delphia set for Gloomhaven, but when I went to buy more, they were discontinued! Arrrugh! I sent an Amazon message to the distributor from my previous order, and was told the Panda sleeves were from the same company. My sets of 1000 sleeves arrived today and I am thrilled! They are the same material, with the same qualities of thin, close-fitting protection, that are not too slick to stack well, and not too matt to shuffle beautifully. And to top it off, the Panda sleeves are 1mm narrower than the Delphia sleeves and so the fit, for games like Arkham Horror LCG, is even better! (see photo) Absolutely my favorite sleeves, by far! The bonus card boxes, with their handy roll of double-sided modeler's tape, is a friendly gesture. Five Stars.

Melissa & Doug Children’s Book - Soft Shapes: Ocean (Foam First Puzzle Book) This is an ingenious first book. It is like a puzzle book. The four puzzle pieces ~ a blue whale, a sea turtle, an octopus, and a seahorse ~ can be removed from the book and played with.

They even go into the bathtub and will float or stick to the sides.

This book is for four months on up. It is not intended for teething.

The colors are vibrant: blue greens, oranges and purples primarily. The ocean animals look cute and friendly.

The text is riddles in the form of who am I? It is rhyming although some of the rhyming is a tad clumsy, but your one or two-year-old won't care.

Here's a sample ~ see if you can guess who it is:

I have eight arms and two large eyes
And really am quite smart
I have no bones and squirt out ink
So predators depart.

The book uses big vocabulary words, but that's good for children to hear. As a former preschool director, kindergarten teacher and principal, I believe in exposing children to big concepts and expand their sense of the world past their everyday experiences. It grows their minds.

This is a gift for our one-year-old for Christmas - it makes for an original gift.

It does say: "Both additives may dissolve and damage the inks in this book." Not sure what additives they are talking about - bathing and teething? It says discard the toy if damaged. That should be made clearer.

4.5 stars
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Children’s Book - Soft Shapes: Ocean (Foam First Puzzle Book)

Matchbox Cars Playset, 4-Level Toy Garage & Tow Truck in 1:64 Scale, Kid-Powered Elevator, Car Repair Station & Spiral Ramp For my 4 and a half year old grandson. He loves his cars and so this was a nice compact "repair garage" play structure. It will not be something you will want to break down daily and store, it will need to be up and available for immediate play. It will stay at my house for his visits and be stored on a closet shelf between visits. It came with one little tow truck vehicle. There is no car storage; this is just a play activity. A turning knob on top of the elevator brings cars up to individual floor levels and there are gates on the ramps that divert the cars to a car maintenance floor and a car wash floor in the structure. Although it says it's 4 level, there is nothing but a ramp from the elevator on the upper level and the lower level is really just the entry to the elevator and an open accessible area underneath that the imagination can invent a use for.

The instructions were also less than stellar and being only in black and white, identifying some of the little pieces was sometimes guesswork. There are small pieces that can be pulled off, so observe the recommended age group for this toy. We were not interested in all the many decorative stickers that can be applied on this toy, so only used what we wanted to.

It appears to be sturdy enough and, if incorporated with some other play structures, could keep his attention for a lengthy period of play time.

text_fidelity_a:
Hape Quadrilla Wooden Marble Run Construction - Vertigo - Quality Time Playing Together Safe and Smart Play for Smart Families,Multicolor This is one of those toys that can provide HOURS of entertainment AND education. You're working those brain cells to build these railways! There's a booklet included with lots of different railways to build. It gives you step by step instructions by picture. You DO have to pay close attention to what color block you place where, and where the holes line up, and how many blocks you use. It all has to line up just right. That said, I wouldn't call this a difficult toy at all. It *will* exercise the mind, though.

I like using it with my 5 year old. It's helping him to follow directions. Of course, I still have to help a great deal. It's also helping him with counting, which he struggles with. It's helping my 2 year old learn his colors. Plus, we're ALL learning patience! ;) These railways fall down pretty easily, since it's basically stacking blocks on top of each other. Honestly, for most 2-3 year olds, I think this thing probably isn't the best idea just yet. For older children, it's wonderful. It has potential to grow with them for *years* to come. This is fun for adults, too! I've had a blast with it.

My ONLY complaint with this thing is the fact that the marbles have nothing to catch them as the come out of the final holes/blocks. They just roll away. We have a 7 month old that crawls everywhere and puts everything in his mouth. We're always careful, but playing with this thing, we have to be extraordinarily careful, especially due to the free rolling marble issue. So far, we haven't came up with a "catching place" for those last marbles, but I'm sure we will in time. We just can't use all the marbles at one time, and keep a close count on what we do use.

The extra caution we have to use is WELL worth it, though!!

This is the kind of toy you just can't go wrong with! (Unless you have children that might choke on those marbles...use your best judgment at that point). Highly recommended from us!
text_fidelity_b: Hape Quadrilla Wooden Marble Run Construction - Vertigo - Quality Time Playing Together Safe and Smart Play for Smart Families,Multicolor

text_fidelity_a:
Klutz Painted Rocks Craft Kit Multicolor, 10.5" Length x 0.75" Width x 8.5" Height This craft kit comes with a book on rock painting, eight acrylic paints, one paint brush, four pairs of self-adhesive googly eyes, and one rock. The kit is for ages 6 and up. The 40 page book comes with instructions on how to use the acrylic paints and included 28 step-by-step instructions for creating various paintings, from animals and flowers to various people, foods, and more. The book also contained pictures of other rock painting ideas but left it to the reader to figure out the steps needed to get the finished product. Most of these were pretty obvious and were similar to previous step-by-step projects.

The acrylic paints are white, black, blue, yellow, red, orange, green, and purple. Some of the designs required mixing these colors to make a new color, and adults may need to help younger kids with this. The paints had something in them to slow the drying time a little (so more like 30 minutes for dry to the touch rather than just a few minutes more typical for acrylic). This allowed for more time to make changes or mixing color on the rock.

The value in this kit is mainly the book as you only get one rock (thankfully...they're easy enough to get locally) and the painting supplies aren't going to go very far (maybe 10-20 rocks?). Still, this kit is enough to see if this is something your child enjoys. I painted the rock in the photo using the book instructions, but modifying the design to fit the rock.
text_fidelity_b: Klutz Painted Rocks Craft Kit Multicolor, 10.5" Length x 0.75" Width x 8.5" Height

text_fidelity_a:
Replogle Aragon 12" Desktop World Globe, Raised Relief, Up-to-Date Cartography, Made in USA (Blue Ocean) The review always asks: What did you use this product for?
Well, when we watch the network news at night, I never know, exactly, where the places are that are in the news.
When I'm introduced to a new person who has an accent I just can't place, and when I ask them where they're from and they answer with the the name of a country, that I'm not familiar with, let alone the continent it resides on, I feel like an ass.
And admit it, when you play Jeopardy (and 90% of the world plays Jeopardy) your palms start to sweat when the category is Capitals Of The World.
And you go into overdrive when the Final Answer is: What peninsula (peninsula?) is where the historic treaty of peace (what?) was signed in 2001 between the United States and the Republic of Whatever (OMG).
This replogle globe, which is Made in the United States, is not only beautiful but it holds lots of information. The Legend denotes swamps from canals and shipping routes. You just can't believe what you can "read" on a globe. If you want to know where they are and you are in this world, buy a globe. Buy this one.
Can you name at least three countries that survive Ukraine?
I rest my case.
text_fidelity_b: Replogle Aragon 12" Desktop World Globe, Raised Relief, Up-to-Date Cartography, Made in USA (Blue Ocean)

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Gaming Monopoly E Electronic Banking What can you possibly say new about Monopoly, the world's favorite property trading game, that hasn't already been said for decades since it's introduction by Parker Brothers in 1935? No matter what new version of Monopoly comes out, it's always so much fun to play with family and friends.

In the sixties, we always had one major problem when the entire family sat down to a long night of playing Monopoly, and that was, we always ran out of money if the game went on long enough. There used to be an office store named Burrows that sold extra Monopoly money and buying an extra packet or two was the only solution to our money shortage.

Now with this new version of Monopoly With Electronic Banking, you'll never run out of money, because there isn't any. The game comes with the standard board, dice, houses, hotels, Title Deed cards, Chance and Community Chest cards, 6 tokens and 6 bank cards that slide through an electronic banking unit which keeps track of your cash on your card. The electronic unit takes 2 AAA batteries (Not Included) and can store millions of dollars on each player's bank card.

It actually takes just as long to type in the money you accumulate on each player's card, as it does to hand count the cash to the players, so don't think this electronic unit is a time saver. We actually found when playing with 6 players, that it saved time to have a separate banker. This electronic banking version of Monopoly may not be faster than the cash version, but it's every bit as fun and that's saying a lot for a game that's been rated number one for over 75 years!
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Monopoly E Electronic Banking

Unusual Suspects Board Game Unusual Suspects is an OK game for the right crowd.

It's essentially an adult version of Guess Who. Twelve cards are placed on the table, and one player secretly chooses one person to be guilty of a crime. Other players ask questions about a character's background or personality, but not their looks or appearance, which the chooser has to answer.

This game can get weird quickly if played with the wrong crowd. Because you have nothing to ask about except an imagined background story, you need to essentially stereotype these characters based on their fashion choices, age, race and gender, and everybody knows it. And as you can imagine, that can be a really awkward experience. In one game, a friend asked "does this character live in a nice neighborhood?" and got a "no" answer, then eliminated the lone remaining African American character based on that answer. We weren't offended, but I'm sure that there are people out there who would be, and those kinds of choices are the meat of this game - you can't ask a question without eliminating a suspect. If you play with people you know, people who are not easily offended, or if you're the type to enjoy a raunchier game like Cards Against Humanity, then this might be right up your alley.

There are 70 suspect cards, and a wide variety of questions to choose from, but the game feels a little underwhelming, even with the right crowd. You can usually make some pretty strong eliminations once you learn which questions you decide to ask to eliminate males or females, young vs old suspects, and once an optimal group strategy is discovered, you can really finish these games incredibly quickly. When it comes down to it, I think the party game market is broad enough that there will always be a better choice for me out there. At the end of the day, there's not too much to bring me back in, and the really funny moments of this game won't necessarily be shared by all.
text_fidelity_b: Unusual Suspects Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
Repos JUST01 Just One, Various There are a lot of "just one word clues" games out there, from Codenames and Decrypto to games like Funglish, Crosstalk or Word Slam, and this game is yet another to add to that group. I think, however, that it's my secnd favorite of the bunch, and if you need a Codenames Killer, this might be up your alley.

In this team game, one player is attempting to guess a word that the rest of their team knows. Each team member writes down one word only, then compares to see if any matches are detected. If they are, those cards are discarded, and the guesser is left with fewer clues. Therefore, the more obtuse clues you get, the more you'll have, but it can be more difficult to deduce the word than if you're given a few obvious clues.

What I like about this game is that it manages to be a louder than usual team game with secrets. In Codenames or Crosstalk, two previous iterations of the concept, games are fun, but often it's players staring at the board in silence. In this one, you still can't say much, but it does lend itself to quicker play, and it's easier to communicate more freely once you have your clues written since your work is done, and the stress of the round is over for the clue-givers. This is a hard game, and it's definitely a word game, but lends itself to being an excellent family gathering game.
text_fidelity_b: Repos JUST01 Just One, Various

WOW! Stuff Collection Fantastic Beasts – Newt’s Light Painting Wand – Award Winner! You will open up a huge world of fun with the Wizarding World WW-1024 Harry Potter's Light Painting Wand, Brown. The Harry Potter wand is about 14 inches long with a grainy wood looking black handle and brown wand part that ends with a very bright LED light tip. The wand has a nice feel and weight to it and seems to be made of a strong resin plastic. The wand comes in a lovely window box with directions, customer support information and a bonus app for making your light paintings.

There is a tiny button on the wand’s handle for turning on the LED light which only stays on as long as you hold the button down. The 3 included 1.5 V LR41 batteries are replaceable by opening the handle end with a phillips screwdriver. This is a great thing, as I can see replacing the batteries often, as our kids can’t put this wand down for a minute. For those of you that look forward to some creative light painting, you will want to download the app. Light painting is just photographing a moving light at a longer exposure shutter speed, in the dark, with no flash. You will want the camera on a tripod to get the light design without shaky movement.

In our house, we can’t get the kids to stop playing with the light painting wand long enough for us to try the light painting. Of course we had to buy another wand, as they play Tag with each other in the dark as well as hide and seek in the dark and casting spells on each other- endless fun for them. I just got one of the wands after bedtime to try a bit of light painting. I only used my camera on the Slow Shutter dial, did not have time to set up a tripod, and snapped a couple photos in the dark with no flash. I caught a photo of the wand making a “V”, and it came out nice for no app or tripod yet. I have seen light painting photos that are fantastic when you know how to manually set your camera for long exposures. Adding a colored cellophane over the light tip makes for gorgeous colored lights too. Our kids love playing with these wands and could care less about the light painting for now. LEGO Star Wars: A New Hope 75244 Tantive IV Building Kit (1768 Pieces) So, I'll admit it. I stayed up most of the night to finish this one. And it's glorious!

This is an adult's plaything. I know, it says 12+ on the box, but that's probably a little young. Make no mistake about that - the manual for this one is longer than most novels that my older one is able to read on her own, and although it is a LEGO product, and her attention span is great for those, this one will challenge anyone, of any age. It's easy to see why - the vast majority of pieces for this one are white, red and grey - and because it's difficult to differentiate between the bits, it can be a bear to put together for the little ones.

Once it's together, this is a masterpiece. The figurines are cool, the detachable roofs of the spaceship allow you to see in and role play the action, and the ship is HUGE. I've put together a lot of LEGO kits lately, and this dwarfs them all.

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Oh My Gourd! Family Game for Boys & Girls Age 6 & Up - A Fun & Fast Family Game You Can Play Over & Over This game is best for really young children! I'd say 2-4. My son is almost 4, but he has some learning delays, so this game has proved perfect for him. Most of the games that are sold in stores, like Wal-Mart are still too old for him. I believe in challenging him, but he just doesn't understand them yet. Again, though, this one has proved to be perfect for him. I've already ordered another game from this line, with hopes to add more along.

There's no type of competition with it. There's 6 wooden snails, a race-board, and two dice. You roll the dice and whatever color they land on, you move that colored snail up a space. If both dice land on the same color, you move that colored snail 2 spaces. Sometimes, I had to wonder what the point was! It IS a great learning tool, though. It teaches taking turns, learning colors, and counting. Plus, quality learning time with children is always a good thing.

While I received this one free for review, I honestly would have purchased it. Before I received it, I didn't even know about this line of games. My son has had fun with it, and I'm really glad that it's now part of our game collection.

Overall, I'd say if your child is very young, or has learning delays, or simply likes simple games, this is a great choice. If your child is used to more advanced games, I wouldn't bother with it. There looks to be more advanced, yet still educational games from this line that might be a better choice, though.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Oh My Gourd! Family Game for Boys & Girls Age 6 & Up - A Fun & Fast Family Game You Can Play Over & Over

text_fidelity_a:
Discover with Dr. Cool PRO Series Rock Tumbler - Turn Rocks into Stunning Gemstones! At first I put this in the kitchen, I quickly learned that it was too loud for an open floor plan, it made me listen to tv on too high of a volume, so when I switched to the 2nd grit I moved it to a spare bedroom. This worked out great since I go in that room almost daily I was able to keep up with knowing when to change out to the next grit.

This is super easy to set up and get started. It comes with absolutely everything needed to go from start to finish including jewelry items to use so you can show off your stones. The instructions are very easy to follow along too.It also comes with activity books and the jewelry pieces are a necklace, a ring, a keychain and ear rings.

The instructions gives you an idea of how long the stones should tumble in each grit and at what speed.
This is what I did..
-grit #1..I did for 3 days on #3 speed
-grit#2.. I started at 5 days on #2…then opened it up and decided it needed a few more days since they were a bit rough so I did 2
more days on #3 setting
-grit#3.. I did for 7 days on #1 setting.
-grit#4..I did 7 days on #1. The smaller stones were great , the larger stones had a few blemishes yet, but I like things when they
aren’t perfect so they were great for me…I will be making them into necklaces once I put holes in them.

As you can see from my pictures from start to finish how much the rocks changed. Then at the end I wiped them off with mineral oil as suggested in the instructions. This has been an amazing experience to watch the rough rocks transform into smooth beautiful stones.
text_fidelity_b: Discover with Dr. Cool PRO Series Rock Tumbler - Turn Rocks into Stunning Gemstones!

text_fidelity_a:
Earthtiles Wooden Magnetic Tiles by Big Future Toys - 100 Piece Set | Montessori Toys | Sensory Toys | Wooden Magnetic Blocks | STEM Building Toys | Wooden Blocks for Toddlers| Toddler Toys Age 3+ [[VIDEOID:2ed5b4ed724fe0fbfda0f1674e634e3d]] Good set of magnetic building shapes with a few thoughts. My kiddo was at a play-date recently, and the friend had a plastic set that the kids really enjoyed playing with. I saw these for review and thought they’d be a great addition to our play area at home. One thing I noticed right from the start is that they sound like baby rattles—you can really hear the magnets moving around inside as you move them. I didn’t notice this type of noise with the plastic ones at the play-date, so just something to keep in mind.

The wood is very smooth and each piece is lightweight. They appear to be durable as I don’t notice any bend if I put pressure on one of the pieces, but they also seem thin at the same time. I’m a little concerned that if someone steps on these by mistake, one of them could crack in half and expose little magnets everywhere. Up until this point, I’ve avoided a lot of toys with magnets, so I’m just going to have to be selective about when we play with these so I can really supervise how they’re being used.

Like magnets naturally do, sometimes the sides won’t link correctly if the positive and negative sides are connected right, so this is a normal learning curve for kids. Otherwise, they stand together very well and there’s plenty of pieces and shapes to build some neat things. These are very nice overall, and if you prefer wooden toys, these are a very good option.
text_fidelity_b: Earthtiles Wooden Magnetic Tiles by Big Future Toys - 100 Piece Set | Montessori Toys | Sensory Toys | Wooden Magnetic Blocks | STEM Building Toys | Wooden Blocks for Toddlers| Toddler Toys Age 3+

Apostrophe Games Blank Playing Cards – 180pcs Blank Playing Cards to Write On – Custom Card Deck with Luxurious Matte Finish – Fun and Cool Playing Cards for Kids and Adults The pack that I got had four bundles of 50 cards - cellophane wrapped. The paper cards are that same size and weight of a inexpensive pack of poker cards that I have (the only difference is the playing cards have a finish applied to them). The blank cards are matte finished and seem to hold ink fairly well with no bleeding. I'm using a variety of pens with these cards - Sharpie permanent markers, Uni-ball metallic gel pens, and assorted highlighters. The gel pens look great and the Sharpies work well too. These cards hold up well under light handling, but start getting a bit ragged over time with heavy use. For what I'm using these cards for (flash-cards, random-number generators, art-card pieces) they hold up adequately for my needs. I will probably be purchasing more of these again in the future.

The only markers I had problems with (that I've tried), were the Sharpie brand flip chart markers. The ink from those beaded up on the surface of the cards and smeared. The highlighters smeared a bit too - but I sort of like the water-color like effect that you can get with using them on these cards.
text_fidelity_b: Apostrophe Games Blank Playing Cards – 180pcs Blank Playing Cards to Write On – Custom Card Deck with Luxurious Matte Finish – Fun and Cool Playing Cards for Kids and Adults

(Also never played but wanted to) So when I got the box and it was barely larger than two boxes of playing cards i went... Well it did say "tiny" on it. I picked up the rules three times and read through them, trying to figure out the solo player game before going "this is not fun to play solo". However we finally sat down and tried out the Tiny Dino game three players. Playing is rather complex involving a small board, cards, and game pieces. It took way longer than the stated 45 minutes, (and TBF we didn't finish all six rounds. Kids quit wanting to play) but that might be because we kept having to figure out order of play, rules and what cards do what. I like the complexity, but it just wasn't a game either of my kids (huge D&D and strategy gamers) liked. They also like rules to be clear, even if complex. So three stars.
One star off because it is hard to read and see in such a small format. One star off because it is needlessly complex, or at least not laid out easily to understand how to play without investing quite a bit of time. Half a star off because one player rules are stupid.
Game free in exchange for an honest review.

text_fidelity_a:
Vector Robot by Anki, A Home Robot Who Hangs Out & Helps Out, With Amazon Alexa Built-In We've been playing with Vector for a little over a month now, and he's a load of fun! At first, he didn't do a lot, but every so often, Anki provides an update and suddenly, Vector has more personality, skills, and interactions! He's a great little desk companion that is much better than a pet because there's little to clean up afterward! I say little because he's been known to shove things off the table!
There are many ways he can learn about his environment via his sensors:
He sees via HD camera.
Facial recognition - he'll learn your face and when he's exploring, will come right up, scan your face, and say your name! He's very pleased when he recognizes you, and gets a little upset if he doesn't recognize you.
Navigate, explore, and learn his environment. He gets around very well all over my desk. However, I move things a lot, so he's constantly having to re-learn. Occasionally, he'll fall over the edge, but once in a while, he falls over the edge. I think they're working on improving that a lot. It's super cute when he's exploring, gets close to the edge, and acts scared and backs away!
If he needs charging, he'll go right back to his charger on his own. However, sometimes, I'll get tired of hearing him causing trouble, so I'll tell him to go to his charger. He does it, but throws a little tantrum when he gets there!

He can hear via his array of four microphones. Sometimes he comes over to see what's going on if you're having a conversation. If he's resting, he'll act startled if there's a loud noise in the room. He will also react to the beat of music if it's loud and near him. If you ask him to look at you or come here, he'll be able to sense the direction to go.

He reacts to touch and feel. If you pet his back, he practically purrs! But shaking him gets a reaction, too!

He has amazing intelligence. For instance, he answers questions, plays blackjack, reacts to his environment, and senses actions and activities around him.

He speaks to you. I'm not a fan of his synthesized voice, but it seems to be improving. When he reads out answers to questions you ask, sometimes it's hard to hear what he's saying. However, as they receive feedback on this, I'm sure his voice will evolve into something more understandable.

We really enjoy seeing his reactions! The current one is the way he gets super excited when you tell him he's a good robot or if you tell him you love him, and pouts a little if you tell him he's a bad robot! I just told him earlier today when he picked up his cube and tossed it off the desk!

I'm super excited to see his ever-evolving skills! I highly recommend this little guy for your favorite tech lover, or yourself! If you're looking for a toy for younger kids, maybe go with a Cosmo. This doesn't have games or things to entertain little ones. But it's completely entertaining for maybe, 10 years and up robotics fans!
text_fidelity_b: Vector Robot by Anki, A Home Robot Who Hangs Out & Helps Out, With Amazon Alexa Built-In

​​​Barbie Playset with 20+ Accessories, Emergency Vehi​​cle Transforms into 2+ Foot Hospital with Lights and Sounds, Care Clinic​​​​​​​​ My 5 year son loves to play with Barbie toys. He uses his stuffed animals and other toys instead of Barbie dolls, though. He greatly enjoys toys with small "real life" pieces, like food and cooking supplies, etc. He was extra excited about this ambulance, especially since his daddy is a paramedic.

There are a few pages of stickers that come unattached. You'll have a bit of effort ahead of you getting all those in the right spot.
